LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 ADVERBS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we show where, how, when and how many times an action occurs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify adverbs in oral and written texts
2. use adverbs to express different meanings correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 ADVERBS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 ADVERBS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify adverbs in oral and written texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify adverbs in oral and written texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify adverbs in oral and written texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify adverbs in oral and written texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use adverbs to express different meanings correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to use adverbs to express different meanings correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use adverbs to express different meanings correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use adverbs to express different meanings correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify adverbs in oral and written texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs to a partner. (skill: use adverbs to express different meanings correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify adverbs in oral and written texts.
3. Practise this skill: use adverbs to express different meanings correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we show where, how, when and how many times an action occurs?
2. What are some of the words you could use to talk more about an action?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Adverbs means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify adverbs in oral and written texts.
5. Be able to: use adverbs to express different meanings correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
